mainTopic: Limits on רבי אלעזר's ruling about an easily altered גט, and a new משנה on who may write a גט
overview: The גמרא first explains that the ruling allowing a גט on a surface where writing is easy to change follows the תנא רבי אלעזר. He holds that עדי מסירה, the witnesses who watch the handing over, make the divorce work, so they can confirm what the גט said. The אמורא רבי אלעזר limits this in two ways. First, the witnesses must confirm the גט right away, in case a condition was erased. רבי יוחנן disagrees and says even days later is fine, because witnesses would remember a condition. Second, רבי אלעזר says the ruling covers only a גט and not other שטרות, based on a פסוק in ירמיהו about documents lasting many days. רבי יוחנן says it covers all שטרות, and the גמרא explains that the פסוק is only good advice. Then a new משנה teaches that anyone, even a חרש, שוטה or קטן, may write a גט, because its validity comes from its signers. The גמרא asks how people without understanding can write a גט, and רב הונא's answer begins on the next amud.

steps.title: This ruling follows רבי אלעזר, who relies on the witnesses of the handing over
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא identifies the source: the ruling follows the תנא רבי אלעזר, who holds that עדי מסירה make the divorce take effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the view of רבי אלעזר, who says that the witnesses who watch the גט being handed over are the ones who make the divorce take effect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering whose opinion lets a גט be written on something that is easy to change. The answer is the תנא רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אלעזר, what counts is the witnesses who watch the handing over, not the signatures on the paper. Those witnesses read the גט when it is given, so they can later confirm its contents. That means a forgery on the easy-to-change surface would be caught.

keyTerms.meaning: Witnesses of the handing over: the people who watch the husband give the גט to the woman
They 'cut,' meaning they make the divorce take effect

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse עדי מסירה (witnesses who watch the handing over) with עדי חתימה (witnesses who sign the גט). For רבי אלעזר, the watching witnesses are what matter, so the signatures do not need to be safe from forgery.
steps.whyThisMatters: Everything else in this section is a limit on this one idea: that we can trust the watching witnesses to confirm what the גט said.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Elazar's view,
phrases.notes: This answers an earlier question: whose opinion allows a גט on a surface where writing can be erased and changed?

phrases.english: who says: the witnesses of the handing over make the divorce take effect.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הִיא, דְּאָמַר: עֵדֵי מְסִירָה כָּרְתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the earlier question about whose view permits a גט on a surface that can be altered.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ruling follows the תנא רבי אלעזר, since he holds that עדי מסירה make the divorce take effect and can confirm what the גט said.

steps.title: The witnesses must confirm the גט right away, out of fear of forgery
steps.stepSummary: The אמורא רבי אלעזר limits the תנא רבי אלעזר's ruling. The גט is valid only if it is confirmed right away, because later the woman might have erased a condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: the תנא רבי אלעזר only allowed it if the גט is confirmed right away. If it is confirmed later, even within ten days, it is not allowed. We worry that the גט had a condition written in it and she forged it by erasing the condition.
steps.whatsHappening: A later אמורא, also named רבי אלעזר, explains that the ruling has a time limit. The witnesses have to confirm the גט immediately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the surface is easy to change, the woman could erase a תנאי (condition) that was written in the גט. If the witnesses testify right away, they surely remember the exact wording. If they testify later, they may have forgotten, so the forgery might go unnoticed.

keyTerms.meaning: Right away, immediately
From now until ten days: some time later, not immediately
We are concerned, we worry
A condition written into the גט
She forged it, she changed it falsely

steps.confusionAlert: There are two people named רבי אלעזר here. The first is the תנא whose opinion is the base ruling. The second is the later אמורא who explains and limits that ruling.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
phrases.notes: This is the later אמורא רבי אלעזר, talking about the earlier תנא who had the same name.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הִכְשִׁיר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אֶלָּא לְאַלְתַּר,
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar only declared it valid right away,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מִכָּאן עַד עֲשָׂרָה יָמִים – לָא;
phrases.english: but from now until ten days — not valid;
we worry that perhaps it had a condition in it
and she forged it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: לֹא הִכְשִׁיר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אֶלָּא לְאַלְתַּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Places a time limit on the ruling identified in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The גט is valid only if the witnesses confirm it immediately. If they confirm it later, it is invalid, because they may have forgotten a condition that she erased.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: even later is fine, because the witnesses would remember a condition
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees. The גט can be confirmed even days later, because witnesses would never forget that it had a condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: even from now until ten days it is valid. If the גט really had a condition, the witnesses would definitely remember it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן argues with רבי אלעזר's time limit. He says the witnesses can confirm the גט even later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that we worry about an erased condition. They disagree only about memory. רבי יוחנן holds that a condition stands out so much that witnesses will remember it, so a forgery would still be caught after a few days.

keyTerms.meaning: If it were so
They will surely remember

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
even from now until ten days it is valid;
because if it were so that it had a condition in it —
they would surely remember.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ מִכָּאן עַד עֲשָׂרָה יָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the time limit set in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The גט is valid even if confirmed days later, since witnesses would remember a condition.

steps.title: The ruling applies only to גיטין, not to other documents
steps.stepSummary: The אמורא רבי אלעזר adds a second limit: the ruling applies only to a גט. Other שטרות must last a long time, based on a פסוק in ירמיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר also said: the תנא רבי אלעזר only allowed this for a גט, not for other documents. As it is written: 'And put them in a clay jar, so that they will last many days.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives another limit. Writing on an easy-to-change surface is allowed only for a גט, not for other documents like sales contracts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ירמיהו about a sales contract teaches that documents need to last a long time without being changed. A גט does its job when it is handed over. Other שטרות are kept and relied on for years, so they cannot be written on something that is easy to forge.

keyTerms.meaning: Bills of divorce
Other documents, such as contracts and loan papers
A clay jar
So that they will last many days

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא רבי אלעזר allows a גט on an easy-to-change surface because the watching witnesses can confirm it. The אמורא רבי אלעזר limits this in two ways. First, it must be confirmed right away, though רבי יוחנן says even later is fine. Second, it applies only to גיטין and not to other שטרות, which must last a long time.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar also said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הִכְשִׁיר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אֶלָּא בְּגִיטִּין,
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar only declared it valid for bills of divorce,
but for other documents — not valid,
as it is written: “And put them in a clay jar,”
“so that they will last many days.”

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: לֹא הִכְשִׁיר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אֶלָּא בְּגִיטִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second limit from the same אמורא as step 2, this time about which kind of document the ruling covers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The leniency covers only a גט. Other שטרות must be written on lasting material, based on ירמיהו 32:14.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says the ruling applies to all documents
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן holds that the תנא רבי אלעזר's ruling applies even to other שטרות, not only to a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן says: even with other documents.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן disagrees with the אמורא רבי אלעזר's second limit from Step 4. He says the same ruling works for every kind of document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 4 the אמורא רבי אלעזר said other שטרות must be made to last a long time, so the ruling covers only a גט. רבי יוחנן removes that limit and says the ruling is valid for שטרות too. This is the second time רבי יוחנן argues with the אמורא רבי אלעזר, after their first argument in Steps 2 and 3.

keyTerms.meaning: Legal documents such as deeds and loan contracts
Even

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan says:
Even with documents.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the limit stated in Step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ruling of the תנא רבי אלעזר applies to all שטרות, not only to a גט.

steps.title: Challenge from the verse about documents lasting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן with the פסוק that says documents should last many days.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it written: "So that they will last many days"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's view using the same פסוק that the אמורא רבי אלעזר relied on in Step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק seems to say that a document must be made to last a long time. If so, how can רבי יוחנן allow other שטרות to be made in a way that may not last? The challenge assumes the פסוק sets a legal requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written? (opens a challenge from a פסוק)
So that they will last many days

phrases.english: But isn't it written:
"So that they will last many days"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's ruling from Step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that the ruling applies to all שטרות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק seems to require documents to last, which contradicts allowing שטרות that might not last.

steps.title: The verse is only good advice
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק gives good advice. It does not set a legal requirement.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the פסוק is only teaching us good advice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן by explaining that the פסוק is advice, not a rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ירמיהו was told to keep the deed in a way that would last, because it was smart to do so. That does not mean a document that may not last is invalid. With this answer, רבי יוחנן's view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Good advice, not a strict requirement
It teaches us
There

phrases.english: There, good advice
is what it teaches us.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם עֵצָה טוֹבָה קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the source as advice rather than law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק requires every document to be made to last.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק only recommends making documents last. It is not a legal requirement.
steps.whatToRemember: The argument between the אמורא רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן depends on how to read the פסוק: as a rule (רבי אלעזר) or as good advice (רבי יוחנן).

steps.title: New משנה: anyone may write a bill of divorce
steps.stepSummary: Anyone may write a גט, even a חרש, שוטה or קטן. A woman may write her own גט and a man may write his own שובר, because a גט's validity comes from its signers.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone is fit to write a גט, even a deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, or a minor. A woman may write her own גט, and a man may write his own receipt. This is because a גט is made valid only by its signers.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that the person who writes the גט does not matter, because the signers are what make it valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives a wide rule: even people we usually do not trust with legal acts may write the גט. It even lets the person who benefits write the document: the wife writes her own גט, and the husband writes the receipt that protects him. The reason is that the witnesses who sign it give the גט its power.

keyTerms.meaning: A deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, and a minor
A receipt, here the woman's receipt that she was paid her כתובה
What makes the גט valid
Its signers (the witnesses)

phrases.english: MISHNA
Everyone is fit to write the bill of divorce,
even a deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, and a minor.
The woman may write her own bill of divorce,
phrases.notes: She writes it and gives it to her husband, and he then gives it to her.

phrases.english: and the man may write his own receipt.
phrases.notes: This is the receipt the woman gives him to show she was paid her כתובה.

phrases.english: For the validity of the bill of divorce is not
except through its signers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic: who may write a גט.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anyone may write a גט, because a גט's validity comes from its signers.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule sets up the question in the next step: if the writer does not matter, what about the requirement that a גט be written for this specific woman?

steps.title: How can people without understanding write a bill of divorce?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a חרש, שוטה or קטן can write a גט, since they lack understanding. רב הונא begins to answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: But they are not people of understanding! רב הונא says:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's list of writers. Then it introduces רב הונא, whose answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט must be written specifically for the woman being divorced. That requires understanding and intention, which a חרש, שוטה or קטן do not legally have. The line ending with רב הונא's name is a setup, and his answer follows.

keyTerms.meaning: People with legal understanding and intention

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the משנה said the signers don't need understanding. The question is only about the writers.

phrases.english: GEMARA
But they are not people of understanding!
phrases.notes: He means the חרש, שוטה and קטן can't have the intention needed to write a גט for her.

phrases.english: Rav Huna says:

steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a חרש, שוטה and קטן may write a גט.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גט must be written for her specifically, which requires understanding that these people lack.
